chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Who owned and managed the Paradise
summary: New Orleans manager Bill Jameison, owners from cigarette vending and general manager Hilda ran the 110th Street club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, this particular thing, but there's a number of questions I still have about the Paradise. Who owned the place and who managed it and what was that all about?

Well, it was people that um...Bill Jameison managed it. He was from New Orleans; he was the manager and he loved music. So that was in our favor. Whatever we did he was all for it. 'Cause most of these New Orleans people, they love music. And he was a New Orleans man'. And I'll never

forget him; he was nice. He was real nice. And then the owners were people that had, they had several...after the war they were in the cigarette vending business and then they branched out into night clubs and the overall general manager of the whole thing was Hilda, a woman. And so...see at 110th Street was a place where there was a conglom-erate of all people and...but everybody came here to have a good time and we had a little show on the weekend and we'd have a shake dancer and a singer. And then durin' the week , like Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday were for the guys to come in and jam, but they all knew that on the weekend we got these people that are workin' all week long and we had to put on a little show.
